name: SalesTarget.ai
summary: B2B outbound platform combining a lead database of 840M+ professional profiles with credit-based enrichment, cold email with no stated cap on connected inboxes (warmup covers 5 on the entry plan), LinkedIn automation, and a built-in CRM and dialer. Sold as separate modules or one bundle per team.
best_for: small sales teams and agencies that want a B2B lead database, cold email with no stated cap on connected inboxes and warmup for 5 of them on Growth (extra slots $2 each a month), LinkedIn automation and a basic CRM under one login, priced per organisation with a few seats included (1 on Growth, 3 on Scale, 5 on Ultimate) rather than per seat
skip_if: you need independent proof of data quality before you buy, because we found no third-party reviews we could read; or your plan is AI-personalised email at volume, because SalesTarget's own AI costs 5 email credits per email; or you need LinkedIn volume from day one, because a standard account takes 42 days of warm-up to reach 20 connection requests a day
honest_knock:
The credit numbers on the plan cards shrink once you read the price list. Unlocking an email address costs 2 credits and a phone number 5, and the help centre charges another credit for adding a lead to a list. Growth's 2,000 credits are therefore about 660 leads a month with a verified email, or about 250 if you also want the phone number. AI-written emails and Copilot draw on a separate pool of AI credits: 100 a month on the $30 and $169 Growth plans, with more at $10 per 400.

The 'Super Saver' badge on the bundle is hard to check. Lead Explorer Launch ($49, 2,000 credits) plus Email Outreach Growth ($30, 10,000 emails) comes to $79 for the same allowances as the $169 All In One Growth plan. The $90 difference buys one LinkedIn account and the CRM, and the LinkedIn tab showed no stand-alone price when we read it, so we cannot tell you whether the bundle actually saves money. The Growth plans now include 1 user; a second costs $20 a month only from Scale up.

Two documents disagree on how to leave. The pricing FAQ says you can cancel any time from the dashboard with no cancellation fee, while the terms say subscriptions auto-renew unless 30 days' notice is given and that partial terms are not refunded. Cancel well before the renewal date and keep a record. The 'Limited Time Only' domain-credit banner across the top of the pricing page is a small thing, but it replaced an earlier 'Labor Day Sale' banner that was still up on 1 October. The LinkedIn side is cautious by design: the help centre starts a standard LinkedIn account at 3 connection requests a day, takes 42 days to reach 20 a day, caps it at 100 a week, and halves your daily limit if fewer than 30% of requests are accepted. We found no independent reviews we could read: there is no Product Hunt listing, and G2 and Trustpilot blocked our reader.

pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-18 on salestarget.ai/pricing and in our own test that day; earlier: re-read 2026-10-28 on salestarget.ai/pricing, tab by tab, monthly billing; the vendor told us on 28 October that its plans had changed. Re-verified 2026-11-12 on the All In One tab and the plan comparison table) Sold either as one bundle or module by module. All In One, the default tab with a 'Super Saver' badge: Growth $169 a month (10,000 emails, 2,000 Lead Explorer credits, 1 LinkedIn account, 100 AI credits, 1 user, warm-up for 5 email accounts), Scale $319 (100,000 emails, 4,500 credits, 2 LinkedIn accounts, 500 AI credits, 3 users, warm-up for 20 accounts), Ultimate $639 (500,000 emails, 7,000 credits, 3 LinkedIn accounts, 1,000 AI credits, 5 users, warm-up for 50 accounts, 3 client workspaces and a one-time $300 wallet credit), Enterprise on request. Lead Explorer on its own: Launch Credit $49 for 2,000 credits a month (1 user), Builder Credit $99 for 4,500 (3 users), Expansion Credit $149 for 7,000 (5 users). Email Outreach on its own: Growth $30 for 10,000 emails a month (1 user, 30,000 contacts stored), Hypergrowth $79 for 100,000 (3 users), Light Speed $299 for 500,000 (5 users) with a one-time $200 wallet credit; new customers get 30% off the first month on any monthly Email Outreach plan. CRM $40 a month with 3 users included and $20 per extra user; Dialer $29 a month with one number and 400 credits, extra numbers $3 local or $5 toll-free. Add-ons on the plans: extra LinkedIn accounts $49 each a month, extra warm-up slots $2 per email account, client workspaces $29, extra AI credits $10 per 400, extra users $20. A 'Customize Yourself' builder prices each part with sliders. The yearly toggle says 'Save 10%' on All In One and 'Save 15%' on Email Outreach; we did not re-read the yearly prices on 28 October. The wallet credits can only be spent on domains bought inside SalesTarget, not on email accounts, and are non-refundable. Free trial: the pricing FAQ says 50 Lead Explorer credits and no credit card. A banner reading 'Subscribe Today & Get $200 or $300 Domain Credit, Limited Time Only!' runs across the top of the page. Payment is by credit card. Salestarget LLC, with an address in Wilmington, Delaware. On 12 November 2026 the All In One amounts were unchanged ($169, $319, $639), and each plan carries an email-volume menu: Growth $169 for 10,000 emails or $199 for 50,000; Scale $319 for 100,000, $389 for 250,000 or $459 for 400,000; Ultimate from $639 for 500,000 up to $2,339 for 5,000,000. The comparison table shows that Growth has no extra-user option, no API or webhooks, no integrations (HubSpot, Salesforce, Zapier, Slack, Calendly, Google Calendar, Zoom) and no MCP server; all of those start on Scale. The Customize builder now prices connected LinkedIn accounts at $49 each for 1 to 15, $39 for 16 to 50 and $29 above 50. The Lead Explorer and Email Outreach tabs did not load without JavaScript on that date, so their prices were not re-read. Read again on 18 November 2026 with a plain fetch: the All In One amounts were unchanged ($169, $319, $639), as were the email volume menus, the 4,500 credits and 3 users on Scale and the banner across the top offering a $200 or $300 domain credit. The Email Outreach tab needs JavaScript and did not load that way, so its cards were not re read; the plan comparison table on the same page lists warmup for 5 email accounts at a time on Growth, 20 on Hypergrowth and 50 on Light Speed, with extra warmup slots at $2 per email account a month on all three, and it states no number of email accounts you can connect. Our reading of 28 October 2026 took the Email Outreach card to mean unlimited email accounts with warmup included; that wording is not on the page now. In our own test the same day, on the Pricing screen inside the app, the Email Outreach Growth card at $30 a month (10,000 emails, 30,000 contacts stored, 1 user, 100 AI credits) read Unlimited email accounts but Email warmup for 5 email accounts, and the add ons listed Extra warmup slots at +$2 / email account / month. So connecting more mailboxes cost nothing extra on the screen we saw, but warming up more than 5 of them does, at $2 each a month. The Hypergrowth ($79) and Light Speed ($299) cards matched the amounts above, the app showed 30% off the first month for new Email Outreach customers and the yearly toggle read Save 15% on Email Outreach and Save 10% on All In One. We did not click Buy Now, and Settings, Subscription showed no active subscription.

compare_with.name: Apollo
compare_with.why: Apollo is the obvious alternative: like SalesTarget it puts a B2B contact database, enrichment and email sequences in one product. The difference is how you pay. Apollo charges per seat: on our reading of 11 September 2026 it had a free plan with 900 credits per seat per year, and paid plans of $49, $79 and $119 per seat a month on annual billing, or $65, $99 and $149 month to month, with Organization requiring three seats. SalesTarget, read on 1 October 2026, charges per organisation with 3 seats included: All In One Growth at $169 a month covers the whole team, where three Apollo Professional seats paid monthly come to $297. That makes SalesTarget cheaper on paper for a small team. Apollo has the free plan, which SalesTarget does not, and a large base of users and reviews you can check before you buy, which we could not find for SalesTarget. Pick Apollo if you want the established option and are one or two people; consider SalesTarget if you are a team of three that also wants LinkedIn automation and a dialer in the same bill.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 18 November 2026 the session tested SalesTarget.ai in the account that we made: a natural language search for marketing agencies with 10-50 employees in the Netherlands set its own filters and showed 532 companies about 2 minutes after the start (real agencies, but also companies that are not agencies), a founders search gave 301, a draft campaign got an AI generated 3 step sequence in about 40 seconds for 1.17 AI credits and was deleted, and the Pricing page was read up to the buy buttons. The Growth plan of Email Outreach lists unlimited email accounts but warms only 5 of them, with extra warmup slots at $2 per account a month. No e-mail or phone was revealed, nothing was connected or sent and no plan was taken. Account and start: we made the SalesTarget.ai account; an earlier attempt on 17 November 2026 stopped on an expired login (the onboarding data could not be saved and the app went back to the login), so it counted for nothing. This test ran on 18 November 2026 with a valid login: our own browser tab was opened at 07:31 on the dashboard of the app (interface already in English). The dashboard offered Earn 20 Free Credits and Continue Onboarding, and the menu listed Lead Explorer, Lists, Campaigns, Email accounts, LinkedIn, Unibox, CRM, Dialer, Validation, Settings and Pricing. The balance before the test was 50 ST credits (a signup bonus of 17 November 2026) and 20 AI credits. Core action, lead search: in Lead Explorer the search bar accepts natural language. The question marketing agencies with 10-50 employees in the Netherlands was entered; after Enter (about 6 seconds, one step) the AI set the filters itself: Company Size 11-50, Country Netherlands and Industry Marketing Services. The result was Total 532 and Showing 1-20 of 532, about 2 minutes after the start. Quality, read by eye: the list holds real agencies, but also companies that are not agencies, such as a flower trade body, a city marketing organisation, a test firm and a marketing training firm. The Country column shows netherlands in lower case, and revenue and other firmographics sit behind a locked View Firmographics button. People mode: the question founders of marketing agencies in the Netherlands with 10-50 employees set Company Size 11-50, Country Netherlands, Industry advertising services and Job title founder, and gave Total 301. It is a mix of agencies and other companies (for example a car-park network and a flyer printer). E-mail and phone are hidden behind View Email (tooltip 2 credits per lead) and View Phone (tooltip 5 credits per lead); neither button was clicked, because that would reveal personal data of third parties and spend credits. No personal name of a lead is kept in the notes or in the images. Campaign and AI sequence: under Campaigns the first campaign Test Project NL Agencies was created (Draft, 0 leads). The editor has the tabs Templates, Leads, Settings and Schedule, a Save button and an AI Sequence Generator that warns This will override current steps created. It asks for the company name, services, target audience, case studies and the number of steps; with test data and 3 steps, Generate showed Generating your personalized sequence and said This usually takes 20-40 seconds. The result appeared after about 40 seconds: 3 steps with Variant 1 and Variant 2, spin options such as Hi, Hello or Hey with a first-name field, and the subject Agency SEO gaps uncovered. Use Sequence was not clicked. No mailbox or LinkedIn account was connected and nothing was sent. The campaign was deleted again through its menu. Credits after the test: ST credits 55 (plus 5 as a bonus labelled Task Completion, Create Sequence) and AI credits 18.83 (the AI Sequence Generator cost 1.17). Lead credits were not used. The test ran from 07:31 for about 10 minutes in all. Plans, read up to the buy buttons: the Pricing page was opened and Buy Now was not clicked, nothing was filled in. Lead Explorer (Launch Credit) is $49 a month with 2,000 credits and 1 user. Email Outreach (monthly, 30% off the first month for new customers): Growth $30 a month with 10,000 emails, 30,000 contacts storage, Unlimited email accounts, 1 user, 100 AI credits a month and Email warmup for 5 email accounts; Hypergrowth $79 a month with 100,000 emails, 3 users and 500 AI credits; Light Speed $299 a month with 500,000 emails, 5 users and 1,000 AI credits. Add-ons: CRM +$40 a month for every user, Dialer +$29 a month, Extra warmup slots +$2 / email account / month, client workspaces +$29 and AI credits +$10 for 400. LinkedIn is $49 per account a month ($39 from 16 to 50 accounts, $29 from 51 to 100), 1 user. All In One: Growth $169 a month (10,000 emails, 2,000 Lead Explorer credits a month, 1 LinkedIn account, Advanced CRM, 100 AI credits, 1 user, warmup for 5 accounts), Scale $319 a month (100,000 emails, 4,500 Lead Explorer credits a month, 2 LinkedIn accounts, 3 users, 500 AI credits, warmup for 20 accounts) and Ultimate $639 a month (500,000 emails, 7,000 credits, 3 LinkedIn accounts, 5 users, warmup for 50 accounts, with a wallet credit applied at purchase). Yearly billing saves 10% on All In One and 15% on Email Outreach. Settings, Subscription said No active subscriptions. Differences with the dossier: the dossier says unlimited email accounts and warm-up included. The Growth plan says Unlimited email accounts, but warmup covers only 5 email accounts and each extra warmup slot is $2 per account a month, so a team that warms many inboxes pays extra. The plan prices that the dossier names (All In One Growth $169 and Scale $319, with 3 users and 4,500 credits on Scale) match the page. No price field is changed here. Checkout: NOT reached, Buy Now was not clicked and no card, total with tax or payment screen was seen. Cancelling: no plan was taken, so there was nothing to cancel; Settings, Account & Settings, Security Settings has a Delete Account button, which was not clicked, and the account was not deleted. Not tested: LinkedIn automation and the 42 day warmup (no LinkedIn account connected), e-mail warmup and mailbox connection, a real reveal of an e-mail or phone number (2 and 5 credits are confirmed only by the tooltips), CRM, Dialer, Unibox, Validation and sending. Clean up: the draft campaign was deleted; the account stays without a plan and without connected accounts; our own tab was closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The list for marketing agencies also held companies that are not agencies, and the founders search mixed agencies with other businesses, so the list needs cleaning before outreach. Revenue and other firmographics are locked, and revealing an e-mail or phone number costs credits. The Growth plan says unlimited email accounts but warmup covers only 5 accounts, with each extra warmup slot at $2 per account a month. The Country column shows the country in lower case.

The dashboard offered Earn 20 Free Credits and Continue Onboarding, and the menu listed Lead Explorer, Lists, Campaigns, Email accounts, LinkedIn, Unibox, CRM, Dialer, Validation, Settings and Pricing. The balance before the test was 50 ST credits (a signup bonus of 17 November 2026) and 20 AI credits. Core action, lead search: in Lead Explorer the search bar accepts natural language. The question marketing agencies with 10-50 employees in the Netherlands was entered; after Enter (about 6 seconds, one step) the AI set the filters itself: Company Size 11-50, Country Netherlands and Industry Marketing Services. The result was Total 532 and Showing 1-20 of 532, about 2 minutes after the start. Quality, read by eye: the list holds real agencies, but also companies that are not agencies, such as a flower trade body, a city marketing organisation, a test firm and a marketing training firm. The Country column shows netherlands in lower case, and revenue and other firmographics sit behind a locked View Firmographics button. People mode: the question founders of marketing agencies in the Netherlands with 10-50 employees set Company Size 11-50, Country Netherlands, Industry advertising services and Job title founder, and gave Total 301. It is a mix of agencies and other companies (for example a car-park network and a flyer printer). E-mail and phone are hidden behind View Email (tooltip 2 credits per lead) and View Phone (tooltip 5 credits per lead); neither button was clicked, because that would reveal personal data of third parties and spend credits. No personal name of a lead is kept in the notes or in the images. Campaign and AI sequence: under Campaigns the first campaign Test Project NL Agencies was created (Draft, 0 leads). The editor has the tabs Templates, Leads, Settings and Schedule, a Save button and an AI Sequence Generator that warns This will override current steps created. It asks for the company name, services, target audience, case studies and the number of steps; with test data and 3 steps, Generate showed Generating your personalized sequence and said This usually takes 20-40 seconds. The result appeared after about 40 seconds: 3 steps with Variant 1 and Variant 2, spin options such as Hi, Hello or Hey with a first-name field, and the subject Agency SEO gaps uncovered. Use Sequence was not clicked. No mailbox or LinkedIn account was connected and nothing was sent. The campaign was deleted again through its menu. Credits after the test: ST credits 55 (plus 5 as a bonus labelled Task Completion, Create Sequence) and AI credits 18.83 (the AI Sequence Generator cost 1.17). Lead credits were not used. The test ran from 07:31 for about 10 minutes in all. Plans, read up to the buy buttons: the Pricing page was opened and Buy Now was not clicked, nothing was filled in. Lead Explorer (Launch Credit) is $49 a month with 2,000 credits and 1 user. Email Outreach (monthly, 30% off the first month for new customers): Growth $30 a month with 10,000 emails, 30,000 contacts storage, Unlimited email accounts, 1 user, 100 AI credits a month and Email warmup for 5 email accounts; Hypergrowth $79 a month with 100,000 emails, 3 users and 500 AI credits; Light Speed $299 a month with 500,000 emails, 5 users and 1,000 AI credits. Add-ons: CRM +$40 a month for every user, Dialer +$29 a month, Extra warmup slots +$2 / email account / month, client workspaces +$29 and AI credits +$10 for 400. LinkedIn is $49 per account a month ($39 from 16 to 50 accounts, $29 from 51 to 100), 1 user. All In One: Growth $169 a month (10,000 emails, 2,000 Lead Explorer credits a month, 1 LinkedIn account, Advanced CRM, 100 AI credits, 1 user, warmup for 5 accounts), Scale $319 a month (100,000 emails, 4,500 Lead Explorer credits a month, 2 LinkedIn accounts, 3 users, 500 AI credits, warmup for 20 accounts) and Ultimate $639 a month (500,000 emails, 7,000 credits, 3 LinkedIn accounts, 5 users, warmup for 50 accounts, with a wallet credit applied at purchase). Yearly billing saves 10% on All In One and 15% on Email Outreach. Settings, Subscription said No active subscriptions. Differences with the dossier: the dossier says unlimited email accounts and warm-up included. The Growth plan says Unlimited email accounts, but warmup covers only 5 email accounts and each extra warmup slot is $2 per account a month, so a team that warms many inboxes pays extra. The plan prices that the dossier names (All In One Growth $169 and Scale $319, with 3 users and 4,500 credits on Scale) match the page. No price field is changed here. Checkout: NOT reached, Buy Now was not clicked and no card, total with tax or payment screen was seen. Cancelling: no plan was taken, so there was nothing to cancel; Settings, Account & Settings, Security Settings has a Delete Account button, which was not clicked, and the account was not deleted. Not tested: LinkedIn automation and the 42 day warmup (no LinkedIn account connected), e-mail warmup and mailbox connection, a real reveal of an e-mail or phone number (2 and 5 credits are confirmed only by the tooltips), CRM, Dialer, Unibox, Validation and sending. Clean up: the draft campaign was deleted; the account stays without a plan and without connected accounts; our own tab was closed. No kit records were entered. A check of this export route with synthetic records, on the account and date stated. Re-importing the export was not tested. The exported file was not opened, so what it contains is unverified. Friction is described, not scored; this is not a verdict on the product.

sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.

claim_checks.observed: The Growth plan of Email Outreach ($30 a month) lists Unlimited email accounts, but also Email warmup for 5 email accounts, and an add-on Extra warmup slots at $2 per email account a month. So the accounts are unlimited, the warmup is not.
claim_checks.plan: No plan was taken; the pricing page was read up to the buy buttons
claim_checks.comparability: The dossier wording against the plan card and the add-on price list; the warmup itself was not run because no mailbox was connected.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: A team that sends from many inboxes and warms them all pays $2 per account a month on top of $30, so unlimited accounts with warm-up included does not hold.

claim_checks.claim: Extra warmup slots +$2 / email account / month
claim_checks.observed: The add-on list on the Pricing page shows Extra warmup slots at +$2 per email account a month, next to CRM +$40 a month for every user, Dialer +$29 a month, client workspaces +$29 and AI credits +$10 for 400.
claim_checks.plan: No plan was taken; the pricing page was read up to the buy buttons
claim_checks.comparability: The add-on prices on the Pricing page against the plan cards; no add-on was bought.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: Add-ons raise the price of a plan: warm slots, CRM seats and the dialer are all extra.

claim_checks.observed: The All In One tab shows Growth at $169 a month (10,000 emails, 2,000 Lead Explorer credits a month, 1 user) and Scale at $319 a month (100,000 emails, 4,500 Lead Explorer credits a month, 3 users, 500 AI credits), equal to the dossier.
claim_checks.plan: No plan was taken; the pricing page was read up to the buy buttons
claim_checks.comparability: The dossier prices against the Pricing page; the prices were not seen on a checkout screen.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: The All In One prices of $169 and $319 a month and the 3 users and 4,500 credits on Scale are as the dossier says.

claim_checks.observed: The AI search for marketing agencies with 10-50 employees in the Netherlands set Company Size 11-50, Country Netherlands and Industry Marketing Services itself and gave Total 532 about 2 minutes after the start. The list holds real agencies and also companies that are not agencies, such as a flower trade body, a city marketing organisation, a test firm and a marketing training firm.
claim_checks.plan: No plan was taken; the pricing page was read up to the buy buttons
claim_checks.comparability: A count of 532 companies against no outside count; only the first page was read and no other tool was run on the same question.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: The list is a start for outreach but needs cleaning; the share of real agencies was not counted.

claim_checks.observed: The people search for founders of marketing agencies in the Netherlands with 10-50 employees set Company Size 11-50, Country Netherlands, Industry advertising services and Job title founder and gave Total 301, a mix of agencies and other companies such as a car-park network and a flyer printer.
claim_checks.plan: No plan was taken; the pricing page was read up to the buy buttons
claim_checks.comparability: A count of 301 people against no outside count; no e-mail or phone was revealed and no person was read.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: The founders list has the same quality problem as the company list; a share of the 301 does not fit a marketing agency target.

claim_checks.observed: The View Email button shows a tooltip of 2 credits per lead and the View Phone button 5 credits per lead. Neither was clicked, because that would show personal data of third parties and spend credits, so the real charge was not seen.
claim_checks.plan: No plan was taken; the pricing page was read up to the buy buttons
claim_checks.comparability: The tooltip text against a reveal that was not done; no credit counter change was seen for a reveal.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: The price of a reveal is known from tooltips only, so the real credit use per contact is not confirmed.

claim_checks.observed: The AI Sequence Generator with test data and 3 steps said Generating your personalized sequence and gave 3 steps with two variants each after about 40 seconds, at the upper end of the stated range. It cost 1.17 AI credits (20 to 18.83) and the ST credits went from 50 to 55 through a bonus for creating a sequence.
claim_checks.plan: No plan was taken; the pricing page was read up to the buy buttons
claim_checks.comparability: The stated time against one generation with test data; the quality of steps 2 and 3 was not read and Use Sequence was not clicked.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: A first draft of a 3 step e-mail sequence comes in under a minute for about one AI credit; whether it reads well enough to send was not judged beyond the first step.

claim_checks.observed: The dashboard offered Earn 20 Free Credits with Continue Onboarding. The balance before the test was 50 ST credits (signup bonus) and 20 AI credits; the onboarding was not finished here, so the 20 credits were not claimed or seen.
claim_checks.plan: No plan was taken; the pricing page was read up to the buy buttons
claim_checks.comparability: The dashboard offer against a balance that never showed the 20 extra credits; the earlier onboarding attempt stopped on an expired login.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: How many free credits a new account really gets, and what they cover, is only partly known.

claim_checks.observed: The Growth plan of Email Outreach shows $30 a month with 10,000 emails, and a banner with 30% off the first month for new customers. Buy Now was not clicked and no checkout, total with tax or card form was seen; Settings, Subscription said No active subscriptions.
claim_checks.plan: No plan was taken; the pricing page was read up to the buy buttons
claim_checks.comparability: The plan card price against a checkout that was not reached; no tax, term or stored cost rule was compared.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: The price you would pay for a month, with tax and the first month discount, is not confirmed.
